findings.title: Unbounded .bot fields drive allocations, rendering loops, and unchecked indices
findings.entry_point: A user-selected .bot file from the desktop game/editor Load actions (ApoBotGame.java:366-367; ApoBotComponent.java:120-133), the fixed files under user.dir/levels (ApoBotGame.java:151-157), or an applet HTTP level response (ApoBotGame.java:153-154).
findings.sink: File-controlled dimensions allocate the two-dimensional array at ApoBotLevelIO.java:79, and menuSize allocates another array at line 94. Parsed menu values cause command-array allocations at ApoBotGame.java:781, 799, and 820; height controls the rendering loop at ApoBotImage.java:114-116; start coordinates reach unchecked indexing at ApoBotComponent.java:541-548.
findings.data_path: Desktop: ApoBotGame.setMouseFunction("gameLoad") -> ApoBotComponent.levelLoad -> ApoBotGame.loadLevel -> ApoIO.readLevel -> ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel. Applet: ApoBotApplet.init -> ApoAppletBufferedStrategy.setComponent -> ApoBotGame.init -> ApoBotGame.loadLevel -> ApoIO.readLevel -> ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel. No field bounds or structural validation occurs before the sinks.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker creates a big-endian .bot beginning with levelCount=1, ySize=50000, and xSize=50000, then convinces the user to open it; alternatively, a malicious server or HTTP interceptor returns it to the applet. Allocation at line 79 exhausts the game JVM. A smaller record can set height to 2147483647 to monopolize rendering or set a 1x1 level's start point to (2,0), causing an out-of-bounds access during rendering. The result is game-process denial of service, not code execution.
findings.preconditions: The victim must open the malicious .bot, run from a directory containing a replaced level file, or use the applet route while the attacker controls its HTTP response.
findings.validation_plan: Run the game with -Xmx64m. Use DataOutputStream to write only the three integers 1, 50000, 50000 to a .bot and select Load; an OutOfMemoryError at ApoBotLevelIO.java:79 confirms the allocation path. For a low-memory proof, write a complete 1x1 record with ground=0, height=0, start=(2,0), direction=2, menuSize=3, and menu values 1,0,0; an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoBotComponent.java:546 confirms unchecked coordinates.

findings.title: Applet level packs are downloaded over unauthenticated HTTP
findings.entry_point: The response body to the applet's cleartext request for easy.bot, middle.bot, hard.bot, or tutorial.bot; it is untrusted when apo-games.de or an on-path network participant is malicious.
findings.sink: ApoIO.readLevel constructs the HTTP URL and consumes connection.openStream() at ApoIO.java:220-224, after which ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel interprets the response as live level state.
findings.data_path: ApoBotApplet.init (ApoBotApplet.java:26-32) -> ApoAppletBufferedStrategy.init sets B_APPLET=true (ApoAppletBufferedStrategy.java:28-33) -> ApoBotGame.init/loadLevel (ApoBotGame.java:151-172) -> ApoIO.readLevel (ApoIO.java:193-224) -> ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel.
findings.attack_scenario: While a victim runs the applet-compatible build, an on-path attacker intercepts the HTTP GET and returns a valid but altered .bot. The attacker can replace the intended puzzle with a trivially winnable level, alter command allowances and displayed points, or return the malformed payload from ApoBot-01 to crash the game. TLS never authenticates the server or protects the response.
findings.preconditions: The applet entry point must run on a compatible legacy Java deployment, and the attacker must control apo-games.de or the network path. Any applicable applet same-origin rule must permit the intended apo-games.de request.
findings.validation_plan: Route apo-games.de through a controlled HTTP proxy or test DNS entry. Serve a structurally valid replacement easy.bot whose visible dimensions, starting position, or command counts differ from the original, then start ApoBotApplet. Capture the cleartext GET and confirm that the replacement level appears in the game; no certificate warning or integrity failure should occur.

findings.title: Applet level reads have no connect or read timeout
findings.code_excerpt:
URL connection = new URL( fileName );
data = new DataInputStream( connection.openStream() );
findings.entry_point: A malicious or intercepted apo-games.de HTTP connection used by the applet level-loading path.
findings.sink: The unconfigured URL.openStream at ApoIO.java:220-221 and subsequent blocking DataInputStream reads, beginning with readInt at ApoBotLevelIO.java:75.
findings.data_path: ApoBotApplet.init -> ApoBotGame.init -> ApoBotGame.loadLevel -> ApoIO.readLevel's URL branch -> connection.openStream -> ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel. The code creates no URLConnection on which it could set connectTimeout or readTimeout.
findings.attack_scenario: The attacker accepts the applet's HTTP connection, sends a successful response and fewer than four body bytes, then keeps the socket open. ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel blocks while reading its first integer, preventing component initialization from completing for as long as the attacker maintains the connection.
findings.preconditions: Applet mode, default URLConnection timeout behavior, and a malicious server or network interceptor able to keep an HTTP response open.
findings.validation_plan: Route the hard-coded host to a test server that returns HTTP 200, sends one payload byte, and leaves the connection open. Start ApoBotApplet and wait longer than normal initialization. Confirm the UI does not finish loading and a JVM thread dump remains blocked below ApoIO.readLevel/ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel until the server closes the socket.

findings.title: Unsigned working-directory levels control win state and point calculation
findings.entry_point: User-editable easy.bot, middle.bot, hard.bot, or tutorial.bot under user.dir/levels, or any .bot selected through the desktop Load dialog.
findings.sink: Parsed ground values determine isLevelWin at ApoBotGame.java:872-880, while parsed menu counts determine totalCommand at lines 781-821; both feed the win flag and point calculation at lines 975-977.
findings.data_path: ApoBotGame.init reads the working-directory file at line 156 -> loadLevel -> ApoIO.readLevel -> ApoBotLevelIO.readLevel -> ApoBotGame.setLevel creates command arrays and totalCommand -> thinkMove calls isLevelWin and calculates points. No signature, trusted manifest, or separation between bundled and user-authored levels appears on this path.
findings.attack_scenario: A local user replaces levels/easy.bot with a valid one-level file containing a 1x1 ground=0 tile, start=(0,0), direction=2, and menu values 100,0,0. After choosing Game and pressing Go without entering commands, isLevelWin finds no GROUND_ORIGINAL tile and awards 2500 points: 1000 + 100*15. This cheats only the local displayed result.
findings.preconditions: The local user can edit the working-directory level file or select a custom .bot. There is no network leaderboard or persistent score in this variant, so the impact does not extend beyond the local session.
findings.validation_plan: Write the twelve big-endian integers 1,1,1,0,0,0,0,2,3,100,0,0 as levels/easy.bot in the game's working directory. Launch the desktop game, choose Game, leave all command slots empty, and press Go. Immediate completion with 2500 displayed points confirms that unsigned level data controls scoring.

findings.title: Unused helper can instantiate classes from caller-selected URLs
findings.entry_point: None in ApoBot as shipped. The only potential inputs are the public path and classname constructor arguments at ApoClassLoader.java:19-21; no other source file constructs ApoClassLoader or invokes getMyClass.
findings.sink: URLClassLoader.loadClass followed by Class.newInstance at ApoClassLoader.java:69-75, which initializes attacker-selected class code if a caller supplies a controlled class path and name.
findings.data_path: The theoretical path is ApoClassLoader(path, classname) -> setPath/setClassname -> getMyClass -> URL construction -> URLClassLoader.loadClass -> newInstance. An exhaustive reference search found no in-variant path from the main method, applet, network response, or .bot parser to this helper.
findings.attack_scenario: There is no reproducible exploit through the shipped ApoBot UI or file/network flows. If clone-and-own reuse later passes attacker-controlled values to this helper, the attacker can place a class with a no-argument constructor at that local directory or applet-mode URL, choose its binary class name, and have its constructor execute inside the game JVM.
findings.preconditions: A new caller, reflective bridge, or embedding application must expose the helper to untrusted path/classname data. Remote URL loading additionally requires B_APPLET=true; desktop mode converts the supplied path to a file URL.
findings.validation_plan: Compile a harmless proof class whose constructor prints a unique marker, place it under a temporary class-directory hierarchy, and invoke new ApoClassLoader(directory, "proof.Payload").getMyClass() from a small harness. The marker proves the sink. Then repeat the source-wide reference search to confirm that ApoBot itself still has no route to the harness call.

notes: All 48 files in the supplied tree are Java source; no levels, images, build files, or Android metadata are present. The corpus extraction preserves an absolute-path-like directory prefix, so the reported paths begin with Users/... but are relative to the supplied SOURCE ROOT. Exact searches found no ObjectInputStream/readObject, MessageDigest, JNI/native declarations, System.load/loadLibrary, credentials, PHP highscore/level endpoints, or sibling-format extensions such as .cheat, .mar, .skunk, .defence, and .rep. The only reachable network input is the applet level URL at ApoBotComponent.java:29. Desktop levels come from user.dir at ApoBotGame.java:156 or the chooser at ApoBotComponent.java:120-133. Points are only rendered at ApoBotGame.java:1283-1285 and are never persisted or submitted, which limits ApoBot-04. ApoIO's generic applet HTTP-output branch at ApoIO.java:166-169 was not reported separately because ApoBot hides applet editor load/save controls at ApoBotGame.java:279-283 and supplies no endpoint to that branch.
